reviewed_by: Claude Opus 5 blind reviewer, re-review after the landmark-distance unit fix, 2026-08-13

samples_reviewed.question_text: A triangle has sides 2 cm, 1 cm, and 2 cm. What is its perimeter?
A rectangle has sides 5 cm and 12 cm. What is its perimeter?
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
A rectangle has sides 7 cm and 1 cm. What is its perimeter?
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.
How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
A rectangular garden is 11 m long and 10 m wide. How much fencing is needed to go all the way around it?
A square has a side of 3 cm. What is its perimeter?
A triangle has sides 2 cm, 4 cm, and 4 cm. What is its perimeter?
Which unit would you use to measure the distance between the barangay hall and the plaza: centimeters or meters?
Which is longer: 2 cm or 12 cm?
The distance from the bench to the tree is 2 m. The distance from the gate to the tree is 3 m. Which distance is longer?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Only six of the sixteen items address perimeter at all: seed 43, 'A rectangle has sides 5 cm and 12 cm. What is its perimeter?', seed 603, 'A square has a side of 3 cm. What is its perimeter?', seeds 42, 46 and 604 in the same shape, and the applied item at seed 601, 'A rectangular garden is 11 m long and 10 m wide. How much fencing is needed to go all the way around it?'. The other ten measure or compare a single length and name no plane figure. Seven of those repeat 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.' or 'How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.', which as rendered carry no object, ruler or figure, so they are not answerable from the information given, and they are not perimeter items in any case.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The measure half of the sentence is well covered across three figure types: triangle at seed 604, 'A triangle has sides 2 cm, 4 cm, and 4 cm. What is its perimeter?', rectangle at seed 46, 'A rectangle has sides 7 cm and 1 cm. What is its perimeter?', and square at seed 603, 'A square has a side of 3 cm. What is its perimeter?', plus the real context at seed 601, 'A rectangular garden is 11 m long and 10 m wide. How much fencing is needed to go all the way around it?'. The identify half has no item: nothing asks the learner to pick out which measurement of a figure is the perimeter, to name the boundary, or to distinguish it from a side. Every perimeter item hands the side lengths over already.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The perimeter arithmetic is right for Grade 2 Quarter 4: repeated addition of two to four small addends with no formula and no multiplication forced. Seed 42, 'A triangle has sides 2 cm, 1 cm, and 2 cm. What is its perimeter?', totals 5; seed 43, 'A rectangle has sides 5 cm and 12 cm. What is its perimeter?', totals 34; and the largest, seed 601, 'A rectangular garden is 11 m long and 10 m wide. How much fencing is needed to go all the way around it?', totals 42, all inside the Grade 2 range. The fencing context is familiar and needs no vocabulary from a later node.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Perimeter is asked in four different ways across three formatters. A triangle with two equal sides at seed 42, 'A triangle has sides 2 cm, 1 cm, and 2 cm. What is its perimeter?'; a second triangle with a different pairing at seed 604, 'A triangle has sides 2 cm, 4 cm, and 4 cm. What is its perimeter?'; rectangles with unequal sides at seed 46, 'A rectangle has sides 7 cm and 1 cm. What is its perimeter?'; a square given by one side at seed 603, 'A square has a side of 3 cm. What is its perimeter?'; and a worded fencing application at seed 601. Distractors sit one or two units from the key rather than repeating.

competency_alignment.rationale: Several items belong to the Quarter 2 length and distance competencies rather than to perimeter of a plane figure. Seed 606, 'Which is longer: 2 cm or 12 cm?', seed 607, 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 2 m. The distance from the gate to the tree is 3 m. Which distance is longer?', and seed 605, 'Which unit would you use to measure the distance between the barangay hall and the plaza: centimeters or meters?', involve no plane figure and no boundary. The seven repetitions of 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.' and 'How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.' are single-length measuring, which is a Quarter 2 action, so the node reaches well outside the sentence it is mapped to.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Where a figure is named the sizes and units fit: seed 601, 'A rectangular garden is 11 m long and 10 m wide. How much fencing is needed to go all the way around it?', is correctly in m for a garden, while the drawn figures at seed 43, 'A rectangle has sides 5 cm and 12 cm. What is its perimeter?', and seed 603, 'A square has a side of 3 cm. What is its perimeter?', are ruler-scale in cm. Seed 605, 'Which unit would you use to measure the distance between the barangay hall and the plaza: centimeters or meters?', teaches that a landmark span takes metres. Two items sit against that same lesson: at seeds 501 and 502 the stem 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.' takes answers of 328 and 259, that is unnamed objects of over two and a half metres reported in centimetres, and with no noun supplied there is nothing to justify holding them in cm.
